transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Time: 11:00 AM PDT (scheduled 45m)
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Sofia Martinez (Prism Retail Lead Eng); Ethan Liu (Prism DevOps); Priya Kapoor (Prism Product); Marcus Green (Prism CTO)

[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team. Ravi and Maya will walk through the SDKs and the Console.
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: Hey, thanks, Jordan. Appreciate it. We're excited — Prism is looking to add a latency sensitive autocomplete and product recommender feature in checkout.
[00:15] Marcus Green: Yeah, want something that feels real time. We care about 100-200ms p50 for small generation calls, cost also matters.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: Totally, that frames it well. We'll do a quick Python/TypeScript quickstart, show auth patterns, then jump into Console and Optimize insights for batching and caching.
[00:35] Ethan Liu: Quick note — our infra is AWS, mostly EKS + Terraform, and we use Hashicorp Vault for secrets. We also have strict PCI controls so any PII/data residency concerns matter.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Noted, we'll surface Dedicated and VPC/private options and KMS/HSM integration.

[02:10] Jordan Blake: Before we dive in, can you share current query volume? rough numbers?
[02:18] Sofia Martinez: We're in prod for search today, about 120 req/s at peak, but the recommender will add maybe another 40-80 small requests per second. Most requests are short prompts ~40-80 tokens.
[02:30] Ravi Patel: Ok that's helpful. For 40-80 req/s and small token size, batching can help cost but we need to keep latency. We'll show continuous batching config and also prefix/KV cache options in the SDK.

[04:00] -- SDK quickstart (Python) --
[04:05] Ravi Patel: All right, opening the Python quickstart. pip install redwood-sdk, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Example snippet:
[04:20] Ravi Patel: "from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-instruct-2", prompt="...")"
[04:34] Priya Kapoor: Sorry, are there separate keys per environment?
[04:38] Maya Chen: Good question. We recommend separate API keys for dev/staging/prod, with RBAC and rotation via Vault or KMS. In Hosted you can create scoped keys; in Dedicated/Private you can connect to your KMS.
[04:52] Ethan Liu: For Vault integration, is there a recommended pattern?
[04:56] Ravi Patel: Many customers put keys in Vault and inject into pod env via CSI or K8s secrets sync; we also support short-lived tokens for CI. We'll follow up with a sample pattern.

[06:10] -- SDK quickstart (TypeScript) --
[06:12] Maya Chen: For TS: npm install @redwoodai/sdk, then import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk' — set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY and client.generate streaming example:
[06:25] Maya Chen: "const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.stream.generate({ model: 'redwood-chat-2', messages: [...] })
stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.text))
stream.on('end', () => console.log('done'))"
[06:45] Sofia Martinez: Is streaming socket-based or SSE?
[06:48] Ravi Patel: We provide HTTP streaming endpoints and SDK helpers that wrap EventSource where helpful; for Node you can use the stream APIs. There are small differences across languages — we'll send you exact snippets.

[08:00] -- Auth patterns and environment setup --
[08:06] Jordan Blake: Authentication options: hosted API keys, SSO for console access (SAML/SCIM), and for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM.
[08:18] Marcus Green: PCI concerns again — do logs ever contain full prompt text? we need redaction options.
[08:25] Ravi Patel: By default we retain metadata for debugging; for enterprise we can enable redaction and disable prompt retention. Private deployments can keep logs on-prem. We'll share SOC2/ISO docs.
[08:40] Priya Kapoor: Can we integrate SSO for the console and still use API keys programmatically?
[08:44] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO is for user access, API keys are for programmatic. You can scope API keys to projects/routes and tie them to user actions in the Console audit logs.

[10:10] -- Console walkthrough (brief) --
[10:12] Jordan Blake: Switching to the Console, you'll see Model Catalog, Routes, and Observability. Let's look at a Route for your recommender: you can pin model versions, add rollout policies, and configure fallback models.
[10:30] Ravi Patel: Observability shows token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency percentiles, and traces to your service. For example, we can set an SLO on p50 and trigger fallback if it's miss.
[10:44] Ethan Liu: Is there an API for metrics export to our DataDog?
[10:48] Maya Chen: Yes, metrics and traces can be exported via webhooks/OTLP; we also have a Prometheus exporter for internal dashboards.

[12:00] -- Optimize recommendations --
[12:05] Ravi Patel: Given your workload, initial recommendations: 1) Use prefix/KV cache for product prompt templates, 2) Enable small-batch windowing (50ms target) to reduce token compute without hurting p50, 3) Consider a quantized model variant for non-critical paths.
[12:25] Sofia Martinez: Can optimize detect quality regressions after a quantized rollout?
[12:30] Ravi Patel: Yes, Optimize ties to evals and your prompt set. It will flag regressions and can auto-roll back if configured. We'll show an eval job example in the next call.

[14:00] -- Code patterns and pitfalls --
[14:05] Maya Chen: A few gotchas: 1) Keep KV cache eviction aligned with user session logic, 2) Watch prompt trimming on long context, 3) For streaming UI, do incremental commit of tokens to avoid double renders.
[14:24] Priya Kapoor: We're using a mix of Next.js serverless and edge functions; any issue with using serverless to call the Redwood API?
[14:32] Ravi Patel: Serverless is fine, but watch cold start latency and secrets handling. For highly latency-sensitive paths, a Dedicated pool or local edge cache may help.

[16:00] -- Integration demo (mini) --
[16:05] Ravi Patel: Live demo — small Node app hitting the SDK with a streaming response. (background typing sounds)
[16:25] Ravi Patel: Ok sending a sample streaming reply, you'll see chunked events appear in the console — that's how we suggest wiring your frontend for autocomplete.
[16:40] Sofia Martinez: Nice. That looks snappy. Is there an example for batching multiple user queries in one request?
[16:48] Maya Chen: Yes, see the BatchRequests helper; we also have examples for grouping similar prompts to improve GPU utilization. We'll attach examples.

[19:00] -- Security / compliance notes --
[19:05] Marcus Green: For Dedicated, do you provide penetration test reports and a SOC2 attestation?
[19:10] Jordan Blake: Yes, we provide SOC2 Type II and can share penetration test summaries under NDA. For Dedicated/Private we offer audit logs and integration with your SIEM.
[19:22] Ethan Liu: For KMS, will Redwood ever hold the unencrypted key?
[19:26] Ravi Patel: No, with customer-managed KMS we only store encrypted material; key policies remain with you. In Private you can use an HSM and Redwood won't have key access.

[21:00] -- Cost conversation --
[21:05] Jordan Blake: Quick note on economics — Hosted per-token pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity. For lower latency and high throughput Dedicated often reduces unit cost, but it requires commit. We'll send a cost model example.
[21:22] Priya Kapoor: What commit sizes do customers usually start with?
[21:26] Jordan Blake: Typical pilot for customers your size starts with a month-to-month Dedicated pilot of a small GPU pool or burstable config; we'll follow up with benchmarks.

[24:00] -- Q&A rapid fire --
[24:05] Priya Kapoor: How do we version prompts and tests?
[24:10] Ravi Patel: Use the Console's evals feature and tie to your Git repo; we recommend automated evals on PRs.
[24:18] Sofia Martinez: Any rate limiting built-in?
[24:21] Maya Chen: Yes per-route quotas and token limits. Also can throttle per-key.

[26:00] -- Final recap / next steps --
[26:05] Jordan Blake: Recap: we'll send pricing/security docs, sample Python/TS snippets including Vault/CICD pattern, and schedule a performance benchmark with the SEs. Customer to share integration repo and CI details.
[26:20] Marcus Green: Sounds good. Prefer the perf session next week if possible.

[27:35] Sofia Martinez: One more small ask — can you include a sample Terraform module to provision a Dedicated ingress with our VPC peering?
[27:44] Ravi Patel: Yep, we have a repo with Terraform examples for VPC peering and dedicated pools, we'll include that link.

[29:00] Jordan Blake: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[29:05] (crosstalk)
[29:15] Meeting ends.
